sentence: This project studies what causes microbiomes in different people to differ in their species, strains, and mutations.
This project studies how lipid metabolism steers the fate of hematopoietic stem cells.
This project tests whether cortical activity that tracks natural speech comes from intrinsic oscillations, evoked responses, or both, using computational modeling.
This project uses genomic technologies and mass spectrometry to find mutated peptides in chronic lymphocytic leukemia and studies how immune responses to them shape it.
This project studies how changes in chromatin and transcription cause skin stem cells to age.
This project tests whether targeted degradation of oncoproteins, alone or with immunotherapy, can fight lung cancer through antitumor immunity.
This project develops an optical implant for multiphoton microscopy to image the murine intervertebral disc over time and study how aging drives degeneration.
This project finds and studies flavin-dependent halogenase enzymes made by bacteria of the human microbiome and builds methods to measure their reaction rates.
This project builds neural network designs that correct biases in deep learning models caused by samples in biological datasets depending on each other.
This project works with communities to put evidence-based cancer prevention and early detection practices into use and to shape policy.
This project uses single cell pharmacogenomics to look for ways to rejuvenate neural stem cells and improve cognition.
This project builds a strategy using machine learning and ecological modeling to predict and prevent bloodstream infections caused by gut bacteria.
This project tests whether acetalated dextran microparticles that bind B cells can cause immune tolerance in an animal model of multiple sclerosis.
This project develops cross-coupling reactions that quickly build fused alkaloid skeletons and uses them to make natural products.
This project studies how bacterial products from gut microbes change gastrointestinal motility.
This project builds a liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry platform to track chemical signaling in organoid models of traumatic brain injury and bacterial biofilm formation.
This project builds a system that combines imaging technologies and artificial intelligence to judge whether donor livers are usable for transplantation.
This project studies acute myeloid leukemia in genetically defined models and tests whether targeting two proteins together helps against subsets of the disease.
This project builds a microfluidic platform guided by artificial intelligence to find and recover rare sperm in men with azoospermia.
This project brings together nanotechnology, bioengineering, and physical sciences groups to develop therapeutic and diagnostic agents for cancer.
